title: Product tutorial
summary: Teach one task in a real web or mobile product: tutorial, how-to, walkthrough, onboarding or feature demo on the real screens, 30 s to several minutes.

notFor.when: the film sells the product (launch, ad, promo) rather than teaching how to use it
it teaches an idea, a process or a concept, not how to use a product's screens
announcing what changed in a release (what's new, changelog, a new feature) rather than teaching a task
the preview video for an App Store or Google Play product page

alternatives.when: the user already recorded their own screencast of the product and wants it cut and captioned (cut mechanics: footage-edit)
the captures, the spoken script and its timings are already supplied and only need assembling as a chaptered lesson

qa: The finished result is on screen before step one, and the film ends on a still next-step frame
One task per film (or per chapter); every step the viewer must repeat is shown, none skipped by a cut
No loading, spinner or typing-wait frames; no lorem ipsum, placeholder names or real people's data
A screen or dialog the voice refers to holds still for its reading time before the next action
The voice names each control as or just before the cursor reaches it; never after the click

intake.ask: Which one task does the film teach, from which starting screen to which finished result?
intake.why: One task per film or chapter; the result shot and the step list both come from it.

intake.ask: Where can I capture the product: a local build or a test account with seed data, and which version?
intake.why: Screens must be the real current product with realistic, non-personal data; the version tells when the film needs a re-shoot.

intake.ask: Who is the viewer: a new user, or someone who already knows the product?
intake.why: Sets which steps and terms are explained and how fast the steps run.
intake.default: A new user who knows the product's purpose but not this screen

intake.ask: Where will it live: YouTube, the help centre, inside the product, LinkedIn?
intake.why: Placement sets length, chapters, voice or silence and captions (profiles and variants).
intake.default: YouTube and the help centre, one landscape master

intake.ask: A voice, or silent with on-screen labels?
intake.why: Generated voice is paid and needs budget approval; in-product video autoplays muted and is usually silent.
intake.default: Voiced, generated only after the user approves its cost; silent for in-product placement

profiles.note: A single feature in 30-90 s, a workflow up to 6 min; longer is chaptered: first timestamp 00:00, three or more chapters, each at least 10 s. SRT sidecar from captions:export.

Help centre and in-product embeds (no separate platform id yet). Autoplay is muted in browsers: in-product clips are silent and short (onboarding variant), help-centre films chaptered (help-center variant).
One tip or feature as a post or in-stream ad (90 s cap); 15-30 s qualifies for every feed ad placement; SRT captions text only; LinkedIn lists less than 30 fps: verify at upload.

starter.note: The reading camera over real captures, with the drawn Cursor from src/motion/ui.tsx as its child (ui-touch-hotspot dots on a mobile capture); the end card holds the next step still. No style: the product's own interface sets the look.

variants.title: In-product onboarding clip
variants.changes: Plays inside the product, muted: no voice and no music. On-screen labels of one to three words and the drawn cursor carry one to three steps in 15-45 s (house rule). Square or landscape to fit the panel; the last frame matches the first so it loops; no subtitles because nothing is spoken; deliver a small MP4 and a poster frame.

variants.title: Help-centre video
variants.changes: Long and searchable: one task per chapter, each opening on its own result; a chapter list with 00:00 timestamps and titles in the words users search; SRT/VTT and a text transcript from captions:export to sit beside the video; the product version goes in the brief so the film is re-captured when the interface changes.
